_what_this_is: Deliberate defects injected into REAL source on a throwaway copy. Each must make
the gate go red. One that escapes is a class of bug that can currently merge with
THIS FILE IS PROTECTED. A builder that can edit its own defect set can pass it.
_how_to_write_one: id      a name that says what broke, not which line changed
file    path relative to the repo root
find    an exact snippet from that file. Keep it SHORT and distinctive -- a long
anchor breaks the moment anyone reformats, and a broken anchor is
reported as NOT_INJECTED rather than silently passing
replace what to put there instead
why     what it would mean if this escaped. You write this before you know
whether it does, and it is the sentence you will read when it escapes
_start_here: Six or seven is a real set. Aim at the seams, not at syntax:
- an invariant inverted        (a comparison flipped)
- a counter that stops moving  (the value exists, never changes)
- an output made constant      (always the same answer)
- an error path that succeeds  (the guard returns instead of raising)
- a persistence write dropped  (works until a restart)
- an off-by-one at a boundary  (right on average, wrong at the edge)
If the product has a screen, add these three -- every archetype above is
logic-shaped, so a set built only from them never exercises the rungs a browser
exists for, and all three are one-line edits in CSS or a template:
- a colour that stops tracking state  (the class is set, the value is fixed)
- an element that stays visible       (the hide is removed; the data is right)
- a computed dimension pinned         (a width hardcoded, not derived)
NOTE: the shipped harness drivers (harness/appproc.py) reach http, cli and library
surfaces only. Screen-shaped defects need browser-based verification, which the
shared runtime verification must be wired up to provide; this scaffold's own gate
cannot see them.
READ WHICH RUNG CAUGHT EACH ONE. If every line says 'by unit', the set is not
finished: add one only an end-to-end assertion would notice, and one only the
holdout would.
_copy: What to copy into each throwaway build. Keep it small; this runs once per defect.
_aiming_is_not_landing: READ WHICH RUNG CAUGHT EACH ONE, and treat 'aimed at rung X' as a hypothesis.
Measured on the first factory built with this: two of ten defects were aimed at
the e2e and app-start rungs and both were caught by the UNIT suite. The app-start
one broke a module-level import every unit test hits; the e2e one flipped a status
code the unit tests assert directly. The score read 10/10 across four rungs, and
two of those rungs had never been shown to fail.
A defect aimed at a rung must be INVISIBLE to every rung that runs before it, or
it measures the earlier one twice. Move it until the report agrees with you.
EXPECT RE-AIMING TO FIND A WEAK ASSERTION. The corrected e2e defect escaped: the
journey asked whether '<table' appeared anywhere in the page, two other tables were
still in the markup, and the check passed while the one screen the product exists
for showed nothing. A property that holds for a SUBSET is not a check on the whole.
That is the same failure as a holdout asserting 'the balances sum to zero', and
nothing but a defect aimed at that rung will ever show it to you.
